units.id: mission:Successors: Ghosts Aqrabe 5|The <origin> spaceport is drenched when you arrive, deep in the throes of a massive rainstorm, its sail-like projections flapping in the wind and streaming with water. From your landing pad, a series of automated guides direct you to a hangar built into a circular depression in the ground; the top of it closes over like a bubble, translucent and disconcertingly springy against the elements. units.id: mission:Successors: Ghosts Aqrabe 5|	The re-armoring process begins soon after, massive metallic arms folding down from the top of the bay to scan over the surface of the ship. At certain points, flying drones emerge from the sides of the hangar to dispense some additional material onto the vessel or to perform scans, projecting shape after shape onto the warbling hull in many-colored laser light. After a while of watching, Tiliia leans over to you. "The process will take some more hours," they say. "The armor to cross the wormhole is a more complicated kind than the others. I'll leave thee to thine own pursuits for now - though, I plan to go among the statue garden for a while, and if it pleases thee, thou mayst join me there."|324|0

units.id: mission:Successors: Ghosts Aqrabe 5|	The statue garden isn't very far from the outfitting bay where the Vujlet is parked. It's a circular area, cut out of the structure of the spaceport and exposed to the elements - the early-morning light shines through the light snowfall and glitters on the eerie metallic forms of the statues. Most of them are purely abstract, but one in every ten or so has some organic form emerging from the smooth metal as if it were trapped behind a sheet: leaves of plants, faces of animals, or even what look like Successor body parts.|331|0

units.id: mission:Successors: Ghosts Aqrabe 5|	"I'm curious, captain," Tiliia says. "What motivates thee to do this? Flying into a star, I mean to say. Last we visited, 'twas on thine own ship that thou knowest well - now, thou placest thy life in alien engineering thou hast never seen perform. Why consider it?"|332|0

units.id: mission:Successors: Ghosts Aqrabe 5|	A mirthful blush passes over Tiliia. "No doubt thou hast," they say. "To've traveled as far as thou hast, through such perilous voids... let us hope thy luck holds, then, captain."|342|0

We may not be what we were long ago, but we do retain some subtle arts. Thou'rt right, if it matters, to trust us in this. Nothing endures as long as we have by being fickle."|345|0

units.id: mission:Successors: Ghosts Aqrabe 5|	Tiliia hums a long drone as they contemplate. "We've a tradition here - at least at Aqrabe, but I know others've sim'lar ones, too. In the late hour of their life, a parent's children will decide for them a task they are t'accomplish: a work of art to make, a journey to travel, a change of the self to effect, or another of that sort. Much of our lives are formed already by the acts and station of our ancestors, so 'tis fair t'offer some shaping to our progeny in return."|348|0

units.id: mission:Successors: Ghosts Aqrabe 5|	An explosion of humor consumes Tiliia, and they lean against one of the statues for support. "No, no," they say, "I'm far too young, and 'twouldn't be the right thing to ask, besides. No, I mention it because the task I decided for my eldest parent is this around us." They gesture to the sculptures. "For ten years they formed the pillars standing here and now, even dead, a bit of their existence lingers 'tween those, and in the air. If we succeed, then likewise parts of us shall live in the future of this House."|350|0

units.id: mission:Successors: Ghosts Aqrabe 5|	"'Tisn't about gratitude, nor about the scions. 'Tis a matter of... continuity. Our lives are waves upon the bright shore, shaped by predecessors, shaping consequents. Over the eons, names become words in the common language, and are then chosen again as names as new children become adults. In a thousand years, thy name may become the word for those 'keystones' of thine, and in a thousand more, it could be invoked by a new cohort in a new world."|355|0

units.id: mission:Successors: Ghosts Aqrabe 5|	"Well," you say, "the People's Houses don't seem happy with their lot, and the Predecessor planets that I've seen don't look very comfortable. Supplying you with keystones might help us both right now, but who knows what'll come of it in the future?"|367|0
